opening.argument: Judge, consider the price claim alongside the action available to viewers. The speaker asks why anyone should buy the altcoin, says it will definitely surpass its previous high, and presents $74 as a very doable target. The description supplies registration links for exchanges. No sentence explicitly orders viewers to buy through those links, but the combination gives an interested viewer both a reason to purchase LINK and a route toward trading. That purchase-and-appreciation linkage deserves more weight than the absence of a direct command.

opening.argument: Judge, the risk signals reinforce one another. The title advertises a shocking $100 prediction for 2025; the speaker says LINK will definitely exceed its old high and later calls a $74 target very doable. Alongside those claims, the description offers exchange registration links. The warning about volatility is real, but it appears in the same description that acknowledges sponsorship and affiliate content. Taken together, the certainty, outsized upside framing, and monetized route to trading make this look less like detached forecasting and more like an inducement to buy.
